name: Helkai
overview: Helkai was a male member of the tribe of Levi, specifically identified as the son of Meraioth. He belonged to the priestly lineage, being a descendant of Aaron, which highlights his role within the religious leadership of Israel. His mention in Nehemiah 12:15 situates him among those who served as priests during the post-exilic period.
namesAndTitles: The name Helkai means "YHWH is [my] portion," reflecting a personal acknowledgment of the Lord as his inheritance and strength. This proper name, recorded in Nehemiah 12:15, is not indicated to have been given directly by God but carries significant theological meaning consistent with his Levitical priestly identity.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records that Helkai was the son of Meraioth, as noted in Nehemiah 12:15. Beyond this father-son relationship, no additional family connections are documented in the biblical record concerning Helkai.
scriptureSignificance: Helkai's importance lies in his role as a priest descended from Aaron, serving during the restoration period chronicled in Nehemiah. His identification among the priests underscores the continuation of the Levitical priesthood and the faithful reestablishment of temple worship following the exile. This connection affirms the ongoing covenantal relationship between God and His people through the priestly service.
